testEnvironment:
Test environment: the snapshot is a git repository whose single commit holds
the reviewed tree — its tree hash was compared against the commit under review
when the snapshot was cut. A suite run here collects and runs what a checkout at
that commit does, so a failing or skipped test is a fact about the tree, not
about this copy of it. Its history is that one synthetic commit: 'git log',
'git diff' and every ancestry question answer about the snapshot and never about
the PR.
The Recipe's Test entrypoint and Check step do not run these merge-gating CI steps, and nothing in this review ran them: Verify branch is rebased on base (needs pull-request context and full git history, not the worktree); Validate renovate.json (fetches renovate from the npm registry via npx on every run); smoke-omp (needs bun and a globally installed pinned omp binary); install-and-smoke (needs bun and a globally installed pinned omp binary).

unverified.claim: The new cases only pin the `.` in `(?<![\w$.])import\s*\(`. A property call with whitespace before the member name, `o . import(name);`, is still treated as a dynamic import and refused, and no accepted case covers that spelling.
unverified.evidence: red: ./agent-test --test-name-pattern='the sweep accepts a gh timeout it can follow beside writes it need not' tests/gh-spawn-bound.test.mjs → exit 1, fail 1 incl 'the sweep accepts a gh timeout it can follow beside writes it need not' (probe case `o . import(name);` added; the sweep reported 'reached through an import() of a path it does not spell out'); baseline: same command on the unmodified tree → exit 0, test pass. This is a probe, not a mutation kill; the source is unchanged by the PR.
unverified.suggested_fix: Add the spaced form `o . import(name);` as an accepted case, together with a source fix (e.g. look back past whitespace for a `.`), or record it as a known limit.
